title: Due-Date Extensions and Unreturned Loaners on Courtesy Transportation Agreements
content:
Desk guidance on extending the due date of a loaner under the Courtesy Transportation Agreements, and on a loaner that stays out after its due date. Each limit named below is the program's own figure.

## Rule

1. The due date is extended only on an agreement in out status.
2. Where the program extends only while the repair order is open, an extension is granted only while the supported repair order is still open (the repair is delayed by parts or diagnosis), never for the customer's convenience once the repair is complete.
3. An agreement may be extended at most the program's most due-date extensions times, and never beyond the program's maximum loaner days after the out date.
4. A loaner still out the program's unreturned-report days, in calendar days, after its due date is reported to police as an unreturned vehicle.

Clause 1 is read from the agreement record itself: the status shown on that same agreement, before the extension is made, decides it, not the customer's description of where the loaner is. Each extension sets a new due date and adds one to the number of times the agreement has been extended.

## Clause 3 as a test on the record

An extension is allowed under clause 3 only when the number of times the agreement has already been extended is below the program's most due-date extensions, and the new due date is not beyond the out date plus the program's maximum loaner days.

| Times already extended | Compared with the program's most extensions | Further extension under clause 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Below the maximum | Less | Possible, within the maximum loaner days |
| Equal to the maximum | Not less | Not allowed |

## Questions the rule answers

**Can the due date of a returned agreement be extended?** No. Extension applies only to an agreement in out status; a returned or closed agreement is not extended.

**The repair order the loaner supports has been completed and the customer would like a few more days. Where the program extends only while the repair order is open, is an extension granted?** No. Under clause 2 the extension is granted only while the supported repair order is still open, never for the customer's convenience once the repair is complete.

**Hypothetical: a program allowing 2 extensions, an agreement already extended once.** One more extension is possible under clause 3, provided the new due date stays within the maximum loaner days after the out date. After that second extension, no further extension is allowed.

**Hypothetical: a program whose unreturned-report figure is 6 days, an agreement due on day 20.** If the loaner is still out on day 26, six calendar days after its due date, it is reported to police as an unreturned vehicle.

The figures in the two hypothetical questions are invented for illustration and are not program figures.
